Examples

slopball — co-op physics soccer with Kit

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Ownership and scoringRun itSolver and presentation timingAutomated tests

Use this Kit example to replicate Godot physics bodies: the ball uses RigidBody2D and the players use CharacterBody2D. play.Puppet connects the ball's solver state to Kit's owner stream. The entity owner—the player permitted to write its owner-controlled fields—simulates the ball and sends its pose and velocity to the other peers.

Ownership and scoring#

Each peer runs move_and_slide for its own CharacterBody2D and streams the resulting pose. Other peers interpolate that pose while keeping remote kickers solid and fixed relative to their local solver.

One peer at a time simulates the RigidBody2D ball through play.Puppet. Its entity owner streams pose and velocity; other peers freeze their solver and follow the stream. The host's proximity arbitration in host.odin transfers ownership to the last toucher, anticipating contact by one step so that the receiving player's local solver can resolve the kick before a round trip. The transfer includes momentum.

The host judges goals from the streamed pose and updates gd:"replicate" fields on the ball. An entity can therefore combine authority-written score with owner-streamed motion, with each field selecting its policy.

Run it#

From examples/slopball, build once with bash ../../build/build_scripts.sh ., then open two windows on one machine:

Shell
SLOP_NAME=lefty  godot --path .    # Host
SLOP_NAME=righty godot --path .    # Join

WASD moves, Space kicks, first to SLOP_GOALS (default 3) takes the match. Odd seats defend the left goal, even the right.

Solver and presentation timing#

The example uses these rules to manage ownership changes and display frames:

  1. Write imposed poses through PhysicsServer2D.body_set_state, as play.Puppet does. Solver synchronization can overwrite direct node transforms on a live RigidBody2D, and unfreezing can discard transforms written while frozen.
  2. Flush the latest sample into the fields before resetting the interpolation ring, then seed the new ring. Kit performs both operations so observers can continue interpolating across an ownership change.
  3. Run the session at the solver's rate: 60Hz here, controlled by SLOP_HZ.
  4. Grant ownership before contact, retain possession across small gaps, and debounce challenges from a moving ball. Idle bodies do not claim it.
  5. Apply accepted corrections to the physics body immediately, then smooth only the drawn skin with a ~63ms half-life. Explicit cuts snap the skin too.
  6. puppet_claim predicts possession when the local screen sees contact. The host confirms or denies that claim; a denial produces a smoothed correction.
  7. Enable physics/common/physics_interpolation=true to interpolate between physics ticks and display frames, and reset it at cuts. Do not linearly interpolate an angle across the ±π wrap.

Automated tests#

  • run.sh — solo gate (SLOPBALL_SINGLE_OK): the striker bot runs the whole loop headless, exercising the 2D physics solver under --headless.
  • native_run.sh — 3-peer integration test (SLOPBALL_NATIVE_OK): host + striker + watcher. The seat transfer lands on all three screens, the striker's local solver scores, and the three screens agree on the ball within a few pixels at the same session tick.
